chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
Whoever makes a mistake in the adhan, and brings something forward or delays it, should return to the first part that he delayed, until he proceeds through to its end.

key_terms.آخِرِهِ: its end, meaning the completion of the adhan
key_terms.أَخَّرَ: he delayed something from its proper place
key_terms.أَعَادَ: he repeated or went back to redo
key_terms.الْأَوَّلِ: the first part or earlier point to which one must return
key_terms.سَهَا: made an inadvertent mistake or forgot
key_terms.فَقَدَّمَ: he put something earlier than its proper place

ai.seo_question: What should someone do if they make a mistake in the order of the adhan?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about mistakes in the adhan. If a person changes the proper order by advancing or delaying a phrase, he should resume from the first portion that was misplaced and continue correctly to the end.
